payload.title: Format into, and parse from, a chosen unit
payload.goal: Add a `unit` option: `format(value, { unit })` and `ms(number, { unit })` express the value in that unit, and `parse(str, { unit })` and `ms(string, { unit })` read a number without a unit in that unit. Keep the 100% coverage the repository enforces.
acceptance: `format(5400000, { unit: 'm' })` is `'90m'`, and with `{ unit: 'minutes', long: true }` it is `'90 minutes'`; the value is rounded to a whole number of that unit, as format() rounds today.
The unit takes any spelling and case the parser takes, such as `'m'`, `'Minutes'`, `'MINS'` or `'hrs'`, and the option is typed that way.
`parse('90', { unit: 's' })` is `90000`; a unit in the string wins, so `parse('2m', { unit: 's' })` is `120000`; without the option nothing changes.
An unknown unit throws an Error that names it, in format and in parse.
README.md documents the option, and both test runs (node and edge) pass with coverage still at 100%.

/bin/zsh -lc "python3 - << 'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path(\"README.md\")
text = p.read_text()
anchor = \"\"\"ms(ms('10 hours'), { long: true })    // \"10 hours\"
"'```"""
assert anchor in text, "anchor not found"
addition = """ms(ms('"'10 hours'), { long: true })    // \"10 hours\"
"'```

### Forcing a Unit

Pass `unit` to express a number in that unit, or to read a unitless string in that unit. It accepts any spelling and case the parser accepts (e.g. `'"'m'"'`, `'"'Minutes'"'`, `'"'MINS'"'`, `'"'hrs'"'`).

```ts
ms(5400000, { unit: '"'m' })                    // \"90m\"
ms(5400000, { unit: 'minutes', long: true })  // \"90 minutes\"
format(2000, { unit: 's' })                   // \"2s\"

ms('90', { unit: 's' })   // 90000
parse('90', { unit: 's' }) // 90000
"'```

The value is rounded to a whole number of that unit, as `format()` rounds today. A unit in the string wins over the option, so `parse('"'2m', { unit: 's' })"'` is `120000`. Without the option nothing changes. An unknown unit throws an `Error` naming it, in both `format` and `parse`."""
text = text.replace(anchor, addition)
p.write_text(text)
print("README updated")
PY'

payload.text:
Implemented the `unit` option for `format`, `parse`, `ms`, and `parseStrict`, plus README docs and a new `src/unit-option.test.ts` covering the new branches (existing locked test files untouched).

decision: `unit` option is typed as `UnitAnyCase` so it accepts any spelling and case the parser takes
decision: format with `unit` rounds via `Math.round(value / divisor)` and reuses the existing `plural()` helper for long forms; `ms` long form stays `"N ms"`
decision: parse with `unit` uses the option only for unitless strings; an explicit unit in the string wins; invalid strings still return NaN
decision: unknown `unit` throws `Unknown unit "X" provided to ms.parse()/ms.format()` naming the passed value
decision: `parseStrict` also forwards the `unit` option for parity with `parse`

What I ran myself: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `jest --env node` 5 suites / 179 tests with 100% coverage, `jest --env edge-runtime` 5 suites / 179 tests. The daemon's post-run test run is the record, not mine.

Did not finish / did not look at: the held-out `src/holdout-unit.test.ts` source (only the name was available); did not run `build`/`attw`/lint beyond a biome check; did not verify publish packaging.
